Items.Authors: Matthias Tecza, Siddharth Maharana, Ryan Griffith
Items.Title: High-dispersion Integral Field Spectropolarimtery: fitting polaristion and spectral orders onto a two-dimensional detector
Items.Abstract: Polarisation of light is a property that tells astronomers much more ddetails about the astrophysics of the objects that their brightness alone. While light from stars is thought to be unpolarised, magnetic fields and light scattering off dust particles, eg in active galactic nucei or atmospheres of exoplanets, imprint a polarisation signature that can be used to learn, for example, more about the size and shape of dust particlaes. The polarisation levels are sometimes very small and hence difficult to measure, and typically only a few polarisation instruments exist at observatories. Similarly, high-resolution spectropscopy has many scientific in astronomy but also requires "bright" targets to measure low-velocity kinematic signals or resolve absorption bands of molecules in stellar or planetary atmospheres.

Items.Authors: Toshihiro Tsuzuki, Ryoko Ishikawa, Yukio Katsukawa, Yusuke Kawabata, Hirohisa Hara, Takayoshi Oba, Akie Moritsuka, Sarah Matthews, James McKevitt, Shota Narasaki, Misaki Miyake, Toshifumi Shimizu
Items.Title: High-fidelity stray-light analysis and control for the EUVST instrument on the SOLAR-C mission
Items.Abstract: SOLAR-C is a solar physics mission led by Japan with contributions from the United States and Europe. Its EUV High-Throughput Spectroscopic Telescope (EUVST) performs wide-band EUV spectroscopy, enabling diagnostics from chromospheric temperatures around 10,000 K to 1 MK and up to 15 MK in solar flares. Because EUV emission is faint, suppressing stray light generated inside the instrument is essential to meeting the requirement of less than 1 photons/sec/pix. We developed a high-fidelity stray-light model using a full structural model of EUVST. The model incorporates diffraction-grating BSDF from electromagnetic simulations, measured BRDF for blackened surfaces, PSD-based surface scattering, and particulate contamination scattering tied to cleanliness levels. These improvements enable reliable prediction of the stray light and support the design of baffling, black coating, and contamination-control. This presentation summarizes the analysis approach, model updates, and key findings.

Items.Authors: Peng Chen, Zhengxiang Shen
Items.Title: High-precision ultra-thin glass sheet stacking manufacturing for multi-channel image slicers
Items.Abstract: The Integral Field Spectrometer (IFS) captures three-dimensional spectral data in a single exposure, saving observation time. Using an image slicer, it provides high light throughput, 100% sky coverage, and stable performance in low temperatures, supporting high-sensitivity near-infrared observations. Deployed in the China Space Station Telescope (CSST), the IFS enables high spatial resolution and wide-band spectral observations. The image slicer, composed of 32 sub-slicing facets (0.25mm width), presents manufacturing challenges. This paper proposes an ultra-precision assembly technique using molecular bonding of multi-layer thin glass and an integrated cutting process. A molecular bonding lens error model analyzes errors, improving manufacturing efficiency by eliminating the interference fringe method. Mechanical and thermal tests confirm the facets' surface accuracy and stability, validating the technique's feasibility for meeting CSST-IFS optical requirements.

Items.Authors: Ko Hosokawa, Takayuki Kotani, Hajime Kawahara, Yui Kawashima, Kento Masuda, Aoi Takahashi, Kazuo Yoshioka
Items.Title: High-temperature transmission spectroscopy system for molecular pressure broadening measurements in exoplanetary atmospheric conditions
Items.Abstract: We present a laser-sourced high-temperature transmission spectroscopy system developed to measure the pressure broadening of molecular absorption lines in H₂&He mixtures at proto-solar composition. This platform enables measurements under gaseous exoplanet-like conditions, where temperature- and pressure-dependent broadening parameters remain uncertain in existing molecular databases. The system employs a tunable laser spanning 1525–1630 nm with up to 0.1 pm resolution, coupled through single-mode fiber into a multi-pass Herriott-cell configuration to achieve a 2.5 m effective optical path. A three-zone furnace stabilizes the sealed gas-cell temperatures between 300–1000 K, while photodiodes monitor the transmitted intensity. This acquires spectra with 0.05–0.5% noise and yields CH₄ broadening widths in H₂&He atmospheres differing by ~30% from database values, enhancing analysis of high-dispersion observations. Ongoing upgrade for CO measurements around 2300 nm will also be presented.

Items.Authors: Vikram S. Dhillon
Items.Title: HiPERPOL: a polarimetry module for HiPERCAM on the GTC
Items.Abstract: I will present the design of HiPERPOL, a polarimetry module for the quintuple-beam high-speed optical camera HiPERCAM, which is mounted on the 10.4m Gran Telescopio Canarias on La Palma.

Items.Authors: Lawrence Bissell, Ellie Smith, Ben Buky, David Isherwood, Jay Stephan, David Lee
Items.Title: Hollow cathode lamps: upgrading astronomy’s calibration lamps for the next generation of multi-object spectrographs
Items.Abstract: Wavelength calibration for multi-object spectrographs (MOS) commonly uses hollow-cathode lamps (HCLs). HCLs provide many well-characterised lines in the visible and near infrared. However, these lamps are too faint for future MOS in the VLT/ELT era, due to the large focal planes that must be characterised. This paper presents a technology development project focused on the design and manufacture of a prototype, high-intensity, HCL unit tailored for astronomical purposes. In our custom-built units we are optimizing the cathode design, material, and current, allowing the mosaicking of configurable cathodes. We also present work on characterisation of Cerium cathodes, identified as a potential alternative to Thorium and Uranium due to its favourable nuclear properties. This work provides a roadmap towards robust, scalable calibration solutions for future spectroscopic facilities.

Items.Authors: Imad Pasha, Roberto Abraham, Deborah Lokhorst, Pieter van Dokkum, William P. Bowman, Seery Chen, Carter Rhea
Items.Title: How to guide a telescope array: control of complex differential flexure via the simultaneous use of multiple guiders
Items.Abstract: We present a novel approach for retaining high pointing fidelity with complex telescope systems, applied to the MOTHRA telescope. MOTHRA is an array of 1140 high-end telephoto lenses equipped with tiltable ultra-narrow interference filters. When completed, the system will be optically-equivalent to a 4.7m f/0.08 refractor with an 8 square degree field of view, operating as an R=800 integral field unit. Its line mapping sensitivity will be an order of magnitude deeper than any other facility. MOTHRA leverages a distributed-aperture design, mounting 38 lenses in a honeycomb lattice on each of 30 fork mounts. Distributed aperture telescopes come with unique challenges, one of which is the complex differential flexure patterns imposed by even rigid honeycomb designs. Here we present and characterize a unique approach, using as many as seven independent guiders per mount, all interlaced together, to actively track and compensate for this flexure, producing high quality, stable guiding.

Items.Authors: Caleb Cook, Nico Deshler, Logan Pawlowski, Amit Ashok
Items.Title: Imaging sub-diffraction star clusters with spatial mode sorting
Items.Abstract: Passive super-resolution imaging using spatial mode sorting has been vigorously analyzed as a technique to approach fundamental limits of resolution. However, a comprehensive experimental validation of this approach has been limited by the fidelity of hardware implementation of spatial mode sorters in terms of throughput, cross-talk, and spectral bandwidth. The recent availability of high-fidelity MPLC-based spatial mode sorters, such as those from Cailabs, enables a comprehensive experimental validation. In this work, we demonstrate sub-diffraction localization of point emitters, emulating star clusters, in various configurations and different spectral bandwidths. Our experiment employs a hybrid measurement method that combines direct imaging and spatial mode sorting measurements. Our measurement model and image estimation algorithm incorporates various error sources such as shot noise, detector dark current, read noise, residual wavefront error, and pointing error.

Items.Authors: Youngchun Youk, Shinwook Kim
Items.Title: Improved MTF measurement for satellite EO cameras using a multi-bar edge target
Items.Abstract: We propose an MTF measurement method for satellite electro-optical cameras using a multi-bar edge target. In the standard knife-edge approach for linear-detector cameras, the target must be scanned repeatedly to collect enough ESF/LSF samples. During this time, small changes in vibration, temperature, and air flow distort the edge profile and increase run-to-run scatter.  Our target combines multiple edge transitions, so one scan provides MTF estimates from multiple pixel groups. This increases the amount of valid data per target movement and reduces sensitivity to slow environmental drift. In our test setup, the method produced more stable MTF results while shortening the measurement sequence compared with the single-edge target scan.

Items.Authors: Eric J. Grigel, David Adriaanse, Grecia Falcon
Items.Title: Improving observatory resilience: insights from Subaru’s 2024 tropical storm damage
Items.Abstract: In August 2024, the Subaru Telescope on Maunakea, Hawai‘i experienced damage to key exterior systems during a severe tropical storm. The event affected the rotating enclosure weatherseals, the coating system on the fixed structure, and the HVAC chiller exhaust outlets that support thermal control. This paper examines the suspected failure modes that contributed to these issues, with a focus on the environmental stresses experienced during the storm. Methods used for damage assessment, diagnostic testing, and repair planning are described, along with the final proposed repair solutions. The paper concludes with lessons learned intended to support improved design, durability, and resilience for future ground-based observatories in remote locations that experience extreme weather conditions.

Items.Authors: Emily Farr, Briana Indhal, Brian Fleming, Kevin France, Dmitry Vorobiev, Fabien Grisé, Nicholas Kruczek, Kristina Davis
Items.Title: Initial optical performance results from the MANTIS SmallSat mission
Items.Abstract: The MANTIS (Monitoring Activity of Nearby sTars with UV Imaging and Spectroscopy) mission is a SmallSat in development at the University of Colorado’s Laboratory for Atmospheric and Space Physics (LASP). Its science payload is built to study high-energy radiation from low-mass host stars and how it shapes the atmospheres of their exoplanets. By observing stellar emission from 100–6000 Å, MANTIS will provide data for understanding radiation-driven atmospheric chemistry and escape. The payload includes two telescopes: a Hetrick-Bowyer grazing-incidence EUV telescope from the Italian National Institute for Astrophysics (INAF) and a Cassegrain telescope for simultaneous FUV, NUV, and optical measurements. We present a mission status update, recent progress from the optical test campaign, and efficiency results for the EUV grating, a first-of-its-kind lithographically etched variable-line-spaced grating developed at Pennsylvania State University.

Items.Authors: Gavin B. Dalton, Lucia Suarez, Ellen Schallig, Roberto Martinez, Joel Conception, Kevin Dee, Judith Santos, Neil O'Mahony, Andrea Henderson de la Fuente, Ian J. Lewis
Items.Title: In-situ maintainance and repair techniques for the optical fibres of WEAVE at the primary focus of the William Hershel Telescope
Items.Abstract: WEAVE is a 1000-fibre multi-object spectroscopy facility at the primary focus of the William Herschel Telescope. The nature of the positioner implies that damage to fibres during operations has a reasonably high probability, and thus the instrument was designed with spare length included for each fibre in the system to facilitate repairs. It was originally envisaged that church repairs would require a full dismount of the instrument top-end from the telescope and substantial downtime necessitating return to Cassegrain observations. However, in operations we have developed access to the instrument in useful orientations at the telescope access park position, and have been able to facilitate all envisaged repair activities in-situ without incurring excessive downtime for repairs.

Items.Authors: David Eglin, Miguel Montesinos-Ballester, Lucius Miller, Davide Pinto, Théa Boussion, Alexei N. Baranov, Roland Teissier, Adrian Glauser, Jérôme Faist, Sascha P. Quanz
Items.Title: Integrated InGaAs/InP waveguides for low-loss astrophotonics between 4-18 μm
Items.Abstract: Molecular absorption features make the MIR range interesting, yet compatible photonic technology remains underdeveloped. The planned space mission LIFE could benefit from photonics in place of bulk optics to characterise exoplanet atmospheres at wavelengths between 4-18 µm. Lighter, more compact and robust instruments reduce mission complexity, while required throughput, bandwidth, and cryogenic compatibility pose technological challenges. A promising photonic platform is InP/InGaAs with low waveguide (WG) propagation losses reported between 4-11 µm and a broad transparency window. We expand our understanding of this platform by measuring waveguide losses at longer wavelengths and under cryogenic conditions. We report on fabrication, simulation, and loss contributions of InP/InGaAs WGs and present a measurement setup with five lasers emitting between 4 and 16 µm. This lays the foundation for future development of integrated astrophotonic circuits operating at long MIR wavelengths.

Items.Authors: Suresh Sivanandam, Ross Cheriton, Robin Swanson, Ryan Dungee, Mark Barnet, John Weber, Jianhao Zhang, Shurui Wang, Martin Vachon, Pavel Cheben, Dan-Xia Xu, Siegfried Janz, Jens H. Schmid
Items.Title: Integrated photonic adaptive optics for next-generation spectroscopic and interferometric instruments
Items.Abstract: Integrated photonic adaptive optics (AO) offers a new path to diffraction-limited performance by replacing bulk wavefront sensors and deformable mirrors with compact, lithographically defined optical circuits. We present an AO system-on-chip (AOSoC) that uses free-space grating couplers to inject the incident wavefront into a reconfigurable Mach–Zehnder interferometer mesh, which performs both phase sensing and correction with nanometer precision. The corrected beam is coupled into a single-mode fibre or routed directly to an on-chip spectrograph, enabling fully integrated AO-fed instruments. We demonstrate closed-loop operation of a 64-element AOSoC, characterize stability and correction bandwidths. Photonic AO promises compact, low-cost, highly replicable systems for multiplexed spectroscopy, optical interferometry, integrated photonic instrumentation, and free-space optical communication, with on-sky demonstrations now being planned.

Items.Authors: Yunjong Kim, Dohoon Kim, Seonwoo Kim, Seunghyuk Chang, Jihun Kim, Yeonsik Kim, Il Kweon Moon, Hyuksun Kwon, Woowon Byun, Yongseok Lee, Sangmin Lee, Jaewon Yoo, Kyohoon Ahn, Jae-Woo Kim, Gayoung Lee, Daewook Kim, Jongwan Ko
Items.Title: Integration and performance verification of two K-DRIFT G1: from laboratory alignment to first-light in Chile
Items.Abstract: We present the development and performance verification of two identical K-DRIFT G1 telescopes, designed as 4.43° × 4.43° wide-field off-axis freeform systems for detecting extremely low surface brightness structures. We positioned each freeform mirror using a CMM for initial placement within tolerance. Tolerance analyses identified the secondary mirror as the optimal compensator. Using interferometric measurements and a wavefront-based alignment method, we achieved residual wavefront errors below 120 nm RMS for both telescopes in the lab. Imaging test in the lab showed point spread function performance within 2 pixels across the field, confirmed at the Bohyunsan Optical Astronomy Observatory in Korea. After deployment to the El Sauce Observatory in Chile, both telescopes achieved on-sky image quality within 1.5 pixels, validating their alignment robustness. These results confirm the readiness of the K-DRIFT G1 telescopes for scientific LSB imaging.

Items.Authors: Mercedes Filho, António Amorim, Paulo Garcia
Items.Title: Integration, testing and validation of the cryostat alignment system for the METIS/ELT WSS
Items.Abstract: The WSS subsystem of the METIS first light instrument for the ELT is being manufactured by the Portuguese team of the METIS Consortium. The WSS consists of three units – ELP (elevation platform and main support structure), RIG (staircase and walkway providing access and maintenance) and CAS (movable hexapod that holds the cryostat with the instrument).  Due to its dimensions, the full integration of the WSS with the rest of METIS will only occur in Chile, during commissioning.   In Portugal, the ELP support ring (main ELP support structure) and CAS will be assembled together with a dummy CRY to simulate the mass of the cryostat with the instrument. In this configuration, the assembled structure will be load tested, and the hexapod control movement will be assessed. We here present the strategy to assemble these two units and perform the required testing and validation.

Items.Authors: Chao Zhang, Hua Bai, Yong Zhang, Xiangqun Cui
Items.Title: Intelligent detection of the motor used in astronomical telescopes control based on artificial intelligence
Items.Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered Intelligent Detection for Astronomical Telescope Motors. AI detection technology has achieved critical breakthroughs in industrial applications, with its core value lying in addressing the inefficiency and delayed response of traditional manual inspections through real-time monitoring and intelligent diagnostics. This study introduces AI detection technology into astronomical telescope control systems, focusing on three primary objectives: condition monitoring, fault prediction, and parameter optimization for optical telescope motors (particularly those in large-scale telescopes). By establishing AI-based fault detection models and parameter identification frameworks, the research enables real-time adjustments to motor controller parameters for telescope tracking, implements hierarchical fault risk warnings, and triggers maintenance procedures. These advancements collectively enhance the telescope's tracking accuracy, stability, and response speed.

Items.Authors: Vikram Seenivasan, Pradip Gatkine
Items.Title: Inverse-designed tapers to improve throughput of on-chip astrophotonic spectrographs
Items.Abstract: Astrophotonics offers a pathway toward compact, miniaturized, stable spectrographs as their size does not scale with telescope diameter. Thus they offer a cost efficient way to achieve astronomy science requirements. A major limitation of current astrophotonic spectrographs is the loss at interfaces between its distinct components, leading to lower overall throughput. We investigate using inverse design to optimize taper-based transitions between components. Our approach explores two methods of fabrication-constrained inverse design. The first employs shape optimization to modify the boundary geometry of the tapers. The second optimizes a gradient region to gradually transform the optical mode between components. This work demonstrates a pathway toward improving astrophotonic spectrographs using computational inverse design methods. This positions us to design high-performance, cost-effective instrumentation for next-generation large and extremely large telescopes.

Items.Authors: Yusuke Munakata, Tatsuya Sawano, Kanaho Okamoto, Atsushi Takada, Yoshitaka Mizumura
Items.Title: KaGErOFU: design of ground-based gamma-ray burst explorer for optical flash understanding
Items.Abstract: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) occasionally show bright optical flashes during the prompt phase, which can reveal key synchrotron parameters such as the cooling and self-absorption break frequencies. However, these flashes often appear and fade within a few seconds, making them difficult to capture with conventional follow-up observations triggered by satellite alerts.   KaGErOFU (Kanazawa University Gamma-ray Burst Explorer for Optical Flash Understanding) is a dual-platform (ground-based and balloon-borne) wide-field system designed to provide pre-planned, simultaneous optical coverage of GRBs. Using 135-mm f/1.4 lenses and back-illuminated full-frame CMOS sensors, tiled to cover about 3000 deg^2, the system reaches a limiting magnitude of 12.6 in 5-s exposures, sufficient to detect optical counterparts predicted by a power law model for typical Swift/BAT GRBs. We report on the system concept and on ground tests with a prototype camera–mount unit demonstrating imaging capability.

Items.Authors: Zhanshan Wang, Jun Yu, Runze Qi, Chunling He, Zhe Zhang, Pengfeng Sheng, Jingjing Xia, Zhengxiang Shen, Bin Ma, Li Jiang, Chun Xie, Xinbin Cheng, Bitao Wang, Chen Xing, Yulei Wang, Xin Cheng
Items.Title: L5-EUV Coronal Imager (LECI): Chinese solar explorer plan to the Sun-Earth L5 Lagrangian point
Items.Abstract: L5-EUV Coronal Imager (LECI) is designed for high-resolution dynamic imaging of the solar corona, enabling reconstruction of the three-dimensional structures and evolutionary dynamics of solar eruptions. In this work, we detail recent progress in the LECI optical system design, mechanical architecture, precision manufacturing and metrology of ultrasmooth mirrors, and the development of EUV multilayer film coatings at the Institute of Precision Optical Engineering (IPOE), Tongji University.

Items.Authors: Aditya R. Sengupta, Dominic F. Sanchez, Benjamin Gerard, Matthew DeMartino, Rebecca Jensen-Clem, Michael Messerly, Paul Pax, Daren Dillon
Items.Title: Laboratory characterization of a multi-photonic lantern optical waveguide using off-axis holography
Items.Abstract: Photonic lanterns (PLs) are waveguides that convert multi-mode input light to single-mode outputs. Wavefront sensing (WFS) and spectroscopy using a PL have been demonstrated, but PL simulations and experiments show significant mismatches. For the WaveDriver project, a proposed Habitable Worlds Observatory pathfinder that uses a PL for WFS as well as for integral field spectroscopy, we manufactured an optical waveguide consisting of seven 19-port PLs in one device. We present laboratory characterization of the individual PLs, consisting of measurements of the principal modes at each PL input using digital off-axis holography. We compare our mode measurements to simulations to assess the variation in the PL manufacturing process. We discuss expected WFS performance in the WaveDriver configuration. This work was performed under the auspices of the U.S. Department of Energy by Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory under Contract DE-AC52-07NA27344. The document number is LLNL-ABS-2013910.

Items.Authors: Tian Lan, Jun Yu, Wenbin Li, Zeyi Ye, Yue Yu, Li Jiang, Chun Xie, Zhanshan Wang
Items.Title: Laboratory-based calibration system for the extreme ultraviolet spectrometer in 55- to 140-nm wavelength range
Items.Abstract: IPOE has developed a laboratory-based calibration system for the extreme ultraviolet (EUV) imaging spectrometer in 55- to 140-nm. Utilizing a RF-produced gas-discharge light source, a grazing-incidence monochromator and an off-axis parabolic mirror to obtain a 50-mm-diameter collimated beam. The system characterizes key parameters of the spectrometer, including dark-field signal, wavelength, spectral resolution, spatial resolution, field of view, system efficiency, and effective area. The calibration process and results are presented and comparatively analyzed.

Items.Authors: Andrea Bianco, Victor Lorit, Demetrio Magrin, Benoit Sassolas, David Hofman, Laurent Pinard, Christophe Michel, Paolo Ciliegi
Items.Title: Large dichroic for MORFEO@ELT: update and perspective
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. One of the key component is the dichroic mirror that reflects the red-NIR light (up to Ks band) and transmits the light at the sodium light wavelength. There are some manufacturing challenges. The size that is of the order of 1 meter in diameter; moreover, the reflection band is extremely wide and the transmission at the sodium light must be very high. LMA has designed the coating with all the constraints and has found a solution matching the requirements. A deep analysis of the niobia as high refractive index material has been performed confirming the possibility to use it in the coating formulation. Some deposition tests have been carried out and the performances evaluated both in reflection and transmission. With these activities, we pave the way for the reliable manufacturing of the finale element.

Items.Authors: Joshua West, Carolyn Atkins, Marcell Westsik, Younes Chahid, Magda Kraus, Sam Tammas-Williams, Nicola Cayzer, Brecht Van Hooreweder, Wenjuan Sun, Mirko Sinico, Sameer Dayanand Meshram, Berk Baris Celik, Daniel Ordnung, Michael Harris
Items.Title: Laser remelting for reduced porosity on additively manufactured aluminium mirrors
Items.Abstract: Additively manufactured aluminium mirrors are fabricated through laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF), enabling the use of complex geometries that provide high strength-to-weight ratios. However, L-PBF frequently introduces pores during printing. This work proposes a novel strategy aimed at reducing porosity, which involves alternating between L-PBF and remelting passes. This is tested on sandwich mirror prototypes, where a field driven design approach is used to generate a lightweight structure that achieves a 50% mass reduction. The influence of remelting on the optical surface is assessed by quantifying the surface roughness, scanning the microstructure, and evaluating the internal distribution of porosity.

Items.Authors: Hanshin Lee, Uma Subash, Matthew Ramirez, Brian L. Vattiat, Joshua Scally, Nicole Wilson, Steven Cadd, Herman Kriel, George Damm
Items.Title: Laser truss edge sensors for the segment-mirror alignment and maintenance system of the Hobby-Eberly Telescope
Items.Abstract: The Segmented-mirror Alignment and Maintenance System (SAMS) is the key equipment that maintains the imaging performance of the Hobby Eberly Telescope (HET) in west Texas. The SAMS constantly measures and controls the alignment of 91 hexagonal mirror segments to form the ideal spherical reflective surface. The existing SAMS (Old SAMS) has been showing its hardware/software obsolescence and aging. In early 2025, our team embarked on the 5-year-long upgrade project to Old SAMS. This “New SAMS” is based on the Absolute Multiline System from Hexagon, which consists of hundreds of laser distance-measuring interferometers and forms an invisible laser truss around the primary mirror to measure critical inter-segment alignment down to tens of nanometer level. In the past year, our team undertook several key activities that include design/development/test of electro-opto-mechanical support systems and control software infrastructure. We detail the outcomes of these Phase 1 R&D activities.

Items.Authors: Diego Ayala Cajas, Roberto López López, Miguel A. Cagigas
Items.Title: LCOS-SLMs applications for adaptive optics and astronomy
Items.Abstract: In this work we present the use of liquid-crystal-on-silicon (LCOS) spatial light modulators (SLM) used for astronomical instrumentation. In our adaptive optics setup, the SLM provides phase and amplitude control to compensate aberrations produced by a Deformable Mirror (DM), and measured with a waveform sensor. The correction had a satisfactory Strehl ratio and point spread function (PSF). Moreover, the Kolmogorov model of turbulence was simulated using an open-source AO framework, allowing real-time manipulation of a collimated beam to reproduce starlight propagation through atmospheric conditions. The SLM also acts as a programmable pupil mask: the combination of optical vortices and telescope-specific pupil geometries (e.g., Keck, GTC, JWST) allow piston and higher-order modes to be introduced digitally to each sub-aperture. These capabilities, together with recent improvements LCOS-SLMs can counteract some disadvantages and make them suitable for future astronomical AO systems.

Items.Authors: Philippe Vallée, Jonathan Saint-Antoine, Lison Malo, Frédérique Baron, Sylvie F. Beaulieu, René Doyon, Étienne Artigau
Items.Title: Lessons learned from a major overhaul of the Observatoire du Mont Mégantic CAmera PAnoramic Proche Infrarouge (CPAPIR)
Items.Abstract: The CAmera PAnoramic Proche Infrarouge, or CPAPIR is a wide field infrared camera that has been used  at the Observatoire du Mont-Mégantic (OMM) since 2004. Time has taken its toll on this very useful camera.  Its detector had one faulty quadrant out of four. In addition, a lot of liquid nitrogen was needed to cool the  camera down and keep it cold for weeks or months. It had become necessary to replace the faulty detector and  also replace liquid nitrogen, as a source of cooling, with a cold head. This paper reports on simulations of finite  element analysis (FEA), 3-D design, hardware selection, and tests that were performed to give a second life to  this workhorse instrument. It also reports on problems and lessons learned during integration and tests.

Items.Authors: Go Murakami, Fuminori Tsuchiya, Atsushi Yamazaki, Umi Enokidani, Masato Kagitani, Shingo Kameda, Kazuo Yoshioka, Masaki Kuwabara, Tomoki Kimura, Ayaka Tadokoro, Ryoichi Koga, Riko Shimizu, Iona Kondo, Ryo Iba
Items.Title: Life-environmentology, Astronomy, and PlanetarY Ultraviolet Telescope Assembly (LAPYUTA) mission: overview of the mission instruments and updates on key technology developments
Items.Abstract: The LAPYUTA mission aims to carry out spectroscopy with a large effective area (>300 cm2) and a high spatial resolution (0.1 arc-sec) and imaging in FUV spectral range (110-190 nm) from a space telescope. The mission unit consists of a Cassegrain telescope with a 60cm primary mirror, UV instruments placed at the focal plane (medium and high dispersion spectrographs and a slit imager), and a fine guidance sensor for attitude control and determination. To achieve LAPYUTA’s requirements, we are developing key technologies including large high-sensitivity tapered microchannel plates, a photon-counting system utilizing CMOS readout via optical fiber, high-efficiency diffraction gratings, and high-reflectivity UV coatings. These key technologies can be applied in future international flagship missions such as the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). This paper will introduce the instrument overview, conceptual design, and development status of the key technologies for the LAPYUTA mission.

Items.Authors: Nicholas Wenner, Joseph H. Silber, Andrew Hope, Michael Schubnell, David Schlegel, William V. Shourt, Robert Besuner
Items.Title: Linear motion flexure (“R-FLEX”) for miniature 6.2 mm pitch optical fiber positioning robots with polar (R-θ) kinematics
Items.Abstract: R-FLEX is a compact flexure-based radial positioning mechanism for next-generation fiber-fed spectroscopic telescope instruments. Designed to fit within a ø5.8 mm package at 6.2 mm pitch—2.5-3x denser than current systems—it delivers ≤5 μm RMS positioning accuracy over a 4 mm travel range. Development utilized parametric optimization, finite element analysis, and fabrication and testing of prototypes. Measured performance met or exceeded requirements across all key metrics. R-FLEX is a promising candidate for mass deployment of precision robotic fiber positioners for future cosmological surveys, supporting the collection of hundreds of millions of galaxy spectra to study the large-scale structure of the universe.

Items.Authors: Jake M. Charsley, William Newman, Yuk Shan Cheng, Derryck T. Reid
Items.Title: Line-by-line control of 10,000 RIZ-band astrocomb lines for spectral flattening and arbitrary shaping
Items.Abstract: High dynamic range in astrocomb spectra leads to a degradation in the wavelength calibration precision for high-resolution spectrographs. We demonstrate a high-resolution spectral shaper that enables independent intensity control of 10,000 lines in a 20 GHz RIZ band astrocomb, providing dynamic spectral flattening and arbitrary shaping at Hz-level update rates. By configuring a cross-dispersing echelle spectrograph with a spatial light modulator (SLM) at the focal plane, spatially resolved comb modes presented to the SLM are individually and arbitrarily modulated. This offers conventional flattening at a higher resolution than typical approaches, with the additional ability to reveal the order-to-order concatenation for wavelength solution extraction and the potential to refine the density of comb lines for improved point spread function analysis.

Items.Authors: Fernando Angeles Uribe, Jorge Fuentes Fernandez, Jaime Ruíz-Díaz-Soto, José Leonardo Garcés Medina, Alejandro S. Farah Simon, Sebastián F. Sánchez
Items.Title: Liquid cooling system for high-stability EMCCD operation of EBANO, a low-cost integral field spectrograph
Items.Abstract: This work presents the design and implementation of a critical subsystem for EBANO, a low-cost integral field spectrograph. While EBANO's main components are 3D-printed, its EMCCD camera requires extreme thermal stability for optimal performance. To address the significant heat generated by the detector's Peltier (TEC) system, the team developed a specialized liquid cooling system. The primary achievement of this system is its ability to maintain an exceptional temperature stability of 0.01 °C at the detector. The summary covers the thermal requirements, the mechanical design of the heat sink, and establishes this cooling system as essential for the success of the EBANO instrument.

Items.Authors: David Blanquez, Jan Petersen, Desiree D. M. Ferreira, Denis Tcherniak, Brieuc De Smet, Giorgio Magistrati, Gabriel Cobos Tello, Alessandro Morello
Items.Title: Lisa PMS: Power Supply Module design and development
Items.Abstract: We present a technical status on the development of the Power Supply Module (PSM) of the Phasemeter Measurement System (PMS) for LISA. We provide a description of the overall module architecture, input and output connections, updated individual component design, specific progress on housekeeping and OVP/OCP circuitry, and an early design of the custom DC/DC converters necessary for the mission’s high demanding requirements.

Items.Authors: Robert J. Harris, Philipp Hottinger, Jonathan Crass, Philipp I. Dietrich, Christian Koos
Items.Title: Long-term performance of the MLR-TT sensor:two-photon polymerization validation in the telescope environment
Items.Abstract: We report on the long-term optical performance of the MLR-TT sensor backed by repeated measurements over the last four years since the sensor was first tested on-sky at the Large Binocular Telescope.  The goal of this demonstration is to assess the feasibility of the underlying technology of two-photon polymerization for future instrumentation in the harsh environment of astronomical telescopes.

Items.Authors: Suijian Xue
Items.Title: LOTUS: L2 orbital telescope for ultraviolet spectroscopy
Items.Abstract: This talk introduces the ongoing conceptual development of a 2-meter class space ultraviolet (UV) mission, featuring high sensitivity, spectroscopy, and pointing capabilities covering the far-ultraviolet (FUV, 90–350 nm) band. It aims to address core astrophysical questions regarding the ionized interstellar/intergalactic medium, hot stellar atmosphere physics, and UV radiation fields impacting planetary environments.    The China Space Station Telescope (CSST), launching in 2027, will leave valuable engineering legacies—silicon carbide mirror blanks, AIT (Assembly, Integration, and Test) facilities, and mission operation experience—for future space astronomy projects. Leveraging these resources, China’s advanced UV mirror coating technologies and recent progress in back-illuminated CMOS detectors enable a feasible, cost-effective dedicated space UV mission, empowering the astronomical community with new capabilities to explore the FUV universe.

Items.Authors: Mark Ferrier, Christian Schwab, David Coutts, Matt Owers, Jacob Pember, Andrew Monson, Chad Bender, David Sand, Duncan Wright
Items.Title: Low-resolution, high-throughput spectrometers for rapid transient follow-up with robotic telescopes
Items.Abstract: Transient astronomy is becoming increasingly important as large-scale survey facilities, such as the Vera Rubin Observatory, identify large numbers of time-sensitive events. The demand for spectroscopic follow-up now far exceeds available capacity, particularly for rapid response. We report on the development of a very high-efficiency, low-resolution spectrograph designed for small to medium (<1.5 m) sized telescopes. Its high throughput allows smaller telescopes to compete with larger facilities, while providing access to increased and more flexible telescope scheduling. It achieves this with affordable system cost, a compact spectrograph design, and broad deployability across existing facilities. Examples for suitable facilities are the robotic 0.8 m MARVEL telescopes at the MERCATOR Observatory in La Palma, Spain, and the robotic 0.8m RAPTOR telescope at Mt. Kent Observatory, Australia.

Items.Authors: David J. Sahnow, Christian I. Johnson
Items.Title: LP-Infinity: overcoming limits to the number of lifetime positions in the COS FUV channel
Items.Abstract: Since the Cosmic Origins Spectrograph (COS) was installed on the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) in 2009, thousands of spectra have been collected with the Far Ultraviolet (FUV) channel. Due to gain sag in the cross delay line detector, regular adjustments to the positions of the spectra have been made, with the seven and eighth becoming available in October 2025. Since the onboard flight software limited the number of Lifetime Positions to eight, it was necessary to develop a new method for implementing additional LPs to avoid reassigning previously used positions. This novel strategy, dubbed LP-Infinity, allows an effectively unlimited number of LPs that is now constrained only by the available detector real estate, allowing COS to continue obtaining high-quality FUV spectra well into the 2030s. We discuss the conception, development and implementation of LP-Infinity, its initial use in Cycle 33, and the plans for future LPs starting in 2027.

Items.Authors: Li Ji, Zheng Lou, Shu Niu, Mingsheng Cai, Wei Liu, Yuan Qian, Shuinai Zhang, Shuping Yan, Keqiang Qiu, Jinlong Zhang, Zhanshan Wang, Klaus Werner, Sebastian J. Diebold, Beate Stelzer, Norbert Kappelmann, Sen Wang
Items.Title: Lyman UV exploration: present and far
Items.Abstract: Lyman UV mapping has historically been limited by the relevant technologies including optical coating, gratings, as well as the advanced detectors. After a decade of explorations in China, we have achieved great improvements in those technological fields. We present here the lab assembling and calibrations of the prototype of the scientific payload of CAFE ((Census of Warm-Hot Intergalactic Medium, Accretion, and Feedback Explorer)) mission, which aims to mapping the Lyman UV emissions (ionized oxygen (OVI) resonance lines at 103.2 and 103.8 nm, and Lyman series) for the diffuse sources mainly for the circum-galactic mediums of the nearby galaxies. We also report the current status of our proposed mission: Lyric (Lyman UV Radiation from Interstellar medium and Circum-galactic medium), as an independent external payload operating on the Chinese Space Station.

Items.Authors: Natalia Arteaga-Marrero, Auxiliadora Padrón-Brito, Adrián Sánchez-Chaves, Diego Tamayo-Guzmán, Max Johann Dobat, Nicolas Lodieu, Jeff Kuhn
Items.Title: Machine learning-driven autonomous control of the distributed aperture for the Small Exo-Life Finder (SELF) Telescope
Items.Abstract: The Small Exo-Life Finder (SELF) is a 3.5 m hybrid-interferometric telescope, designed as a prototype for the future Exo-Life Finder (ELF), a next-generation telescope aimed at detecting bio- and technosignatures through direct imaging. SELF comprises a distributed interferometric array of 15 independently controlled primary mirrors, each paired with a secondary. The system’s complex optical and mechanical degrees of freedom require machine-learning-driven control for precise alignment. Convolutional neural networks were implemented to map these degrees of freedom to control signals. Validation with synthetic datasets from a detailed telescope model demonstrates that the approach accurately retrieves tilt perturbations from residual features in interference patterns, maintaining performance under degraded conditions. These results enable system sensitivity analysis and optimization of alignment strategies, facilitating the transition to full coherence.

Items.Authors: Natalia Auricchio, Joseph Huesler, Simonetta Chinellato, Daniele Brienza, Gonzalo Ramos Zapata, Fernando Conde García, Amaia Santiago Pé, Lionel Lourit, Nathalie Gorter, Ricardo Bolt, Aline Hermans, Ilina Kondofersky, Giacomo Cherchi, Nicolas Gorius, Gianalfredo Nicolini, Flavia Calderone, Isabella Pagano, Elisabetta Tommasi
Items.Title: Management of the product assurance activities for PLATO camera
Items.Abstract: PLATO (PLAnetary Transits and Oscillations of stars) is an M3 medium-class space mission in ESA Cosmic Vision program devoted to detecting and studying a large number of extrasolar planetary systems. The launch window is planned for early 2027 from Europe’s Spaceport in French Guiana. The Payload includes 26 wide field-of-view Cameras, each observing a specific part of the sky, with the associated data processing units and power supply units. All 26 cameras were delivered to the Prime and integrated into the Optical Bench. The PLM was successfully connected to the SVM, which houses the systems operating the spacecraft.   This work outlines the status of Product Assurance activities at the end of serial production, when the cameras were shipped to the Prime, and in preparation for the AR. Specifically, we will describe the dedicated PA/QA structure that has been established to meet the project specific requirements, including the inspections, NCRs/RFXs management and cleanliness control.

Items.Authors: GyeongGon Bahk, Yunjong Kim, Jihun Kim, Heuisung Cho, Seunghyuk Chang, Dohoon Kim, Kyohoon Ahn, Il Kweon Moon, Yeonsik Kim, Hyuksun Kwon, Daewook Kim, Woowon Byun, Kwang-Il Seon, Yongseok Lee, Sangmin Lee, Sang-Mok Cha, Jongyeob Park, Hong Soo Park, Gayoung Lee, Seonwoo Kim, Seri Yeon, Jongwan Ko
Items.Title: Manufacturable tolerance budgets for the K-DRIFT G2
Items.Abstract: KASI Deep Rolling Imaging Fast Telescope Generation 2 (K-DRIFT G2) is a Linear Astigmatism-Free Three-Mirror System (LAF-TMS) utilizing off-axis freeform optics, designed for a sounding rocket mission to observe Low Surface Brightness (LSB) objects. A Dichroic Beam Splitter (DBS) has been added to the system for simultaneous observation of UV and visible light; the UV light reflects at DBS, while the visible light transmits at DBS. The rear surface of DBS configured to correct residual aberrations of transmitted visible light through its freeform shape. In essence, K-DRIFT G2 has become an optical system where all components are composed of freeform surfaces, leading to expected high technical difficulty in the actual fabrication process. Therefore, this study aims to discuss the procedure for establishing the tolerance budget for the efficient fabrication of this all-component off-axis freeform optical system.

Items.Authors: Warren B. Foster, Roger Angel, Chad F. Bender, Gilberto Chavez Lopez, Kevin Gilliam, Peter Gray, Andy Monson, Jason Patrou, Peter Shea, Melanie Sisco, Richard Wortley
Items.Title: Mass production of the LFAST 0.76m primary mirrors: fabrication tradeoffs and on-sky control
Items.Abstract: The Large Fiber Array Spectroscopic Telescope provides large collecting aperture at low cost. Individual 0.76m, f/3.3 spherical mirrors focus light into fibers that combine at a central spectrograph. Mirrors are slumped, ground on Trizact pads and polished on pitch using interferometric metrology. A large 32:1 aspect ratio was chosen to reduce material cost but leads to characteristic print-through errors. We present a process that balances tradeoffs between different fabrication methods to achieve 80% encircled energy in a 1.4arcsec fiber within a one-week cycle time.  Twenty mirrors are integrated onto a common tracking mount and supported with passive whiffle trees. While on-sky, gravity vector and thermal variations cause figure errors that are measured with focal plane wavefront sensing and corrected with perimeter Peltier devices. This 20x prototype will have a 3.4m equivalent collecting area and establishes a roadmap towards a future order of magnitude increase in aperture size.

Items.Authors: Simone Doniselli, Matteo Aliverti
Items.Title: MAVIS: cooling deformable mirrors using a Ranque–Hilsch vortex tube: prototyping and performance assessment
Items.Abstract: This work presents the prototyping and performance characterization of a Ranque–Hilsch Vortex Tube (RHVT) cooling concept for the deformable mirrors of the MAVIS Adaptive Optics Module. Tests conducted under the flow-limited conditions of the VLT infrastructure show that RHVT performance depends strongly on cold-mass fraction, inlet flow, and downstream pressure. Temperature drops of ~–20 °C and cooling powers of ~8 W were achieved, meeting MAVIS requirements. The results confirm that RHVT cooling is feasible if carefully tuned and integrated with appropriate pipeline sizing, insulation, and on-site calibration.

Items.Authors: Simone Doniselli, Matteo Aliverti, Davide Greggio
Items.Title: MAVIS: mechanical characterization of binding materials for cemented optics under thermal stress
Items.Abstract: This work presents a systematic mechanical characterization of silicone- and epoxy-based polymeric binding materials used in cemented optics. Using BK7 samples tested under controlled shear loading and relaxation, we derived shear modulus and viscoelastic parameters as a function of adhesive-layer thickness. Silicone materials showed thickness-independent mechanical behavior, while epoxies exhibited strong thickness dependence. The very low viscoelastic index (~10⁻³) confirms that linear elasticity is adequate for most analyses. These results provide practical guidelines for selecting and modelling adhesives in thermally stressed astronomical optical assemblies.

Items.Authors: Derya Öztürk Çetni, Taner Tarıık Aytaş, Ersen Balcı, Ebru Uzunçam, Naime Sude Börekçi, İlayda Ekinci, Dilara Demirci, Bilal Arslan, Muhammed Baki Bayram, Elif Temel, Berkay Şahin, Gizay Yolalan, Ramazan Şahin, Cahit Yeşilyaprak
Items.Title: Measurement of controlled turbulence effects on the optical path and Zernike modal analysis in a laboratory environment
Items.Abstract: This study aims to evaluate the performance of optical systems under laboratory-controlled atmospheric turbulence. A collimated beam passes through a turbulence generator, and the resulting wavefront distortions are measured using a Shack-Hartmann WFS. Along the same path, a focal plane camera records the beam profiles, which are analyzed in terms of Cn² and Zernike modes. This approach allows for systematic turbulence control and comparison with theoretical models.   The results evaluate the effect of turbulence on performance by revealing correlations between the Zernike modes obtained from the WFS and the focal plane images. The work provides a laboratory framework for investigating the contribution of varying turbulence conditions to the low-order Zernike aberrations typically associated with active optics in medium and large aperture telescopes.

Items.Authors: Richard Massey, Jacob A. Kegerreis, Juan Paolo Lorenzo Gerardo Barrios, James W. Nightingale, Richard G. Hayes, David Lagattuta, Zane D. Lentz, Gavin Leroy, Jesper Skottfelt, Felix Vecchi, Maximilian von Wietersheim-Kramsta
Items.Title: Measuring radiation damage to the Hubble Space Telescope over 23 years and correcting it using ArCTIc
Items.Abstract: Since its launch, the Hubble Space Telescope’s Advanced Camera for Surveys (ACS) has been exposed to damaging radiation above the atmosphere. We track the degradation of the ACS’ image quality and find the rate of damage to be modulated by 18.5% during an 11-year solar cycle, peaking 430 days after (i.e. out of phase with) solar minimum based on the number of sunspots. We also find that the type of damage is consistent with defects in the silicon lattice that have all stabilised into one of three configurations. To correct for radiation damage in ACS images, we present the Algorithm for Charge Transfer Inefficiency correction (ArCTIc) v7. It models the physical processes that cause radiation damage to manifest in images. By calibrating ArCTIc using the trailing from ‘hot pixels’ and applying it to astronomical images, we correct 99.9 % of trailing in the worst-affected recent data and 99.5% of trailing averaged over the ACS’s lifetime.

Items.Authors: Christian Schwab, Glen Douglass, David Coutts, Dane Zielinski-Nicolson, Julian Stuermer
Items.Title: Measuring the dispersion of an etalon for wavelength calibration using an optical spectrum analyser
Items.Abstract: The performance of etalon-based calibration sources for precision spectroscopy depends on understanding their intrinsic dispersion and how that dispersion evolves over time. This work presents a practical methodology for measuring etalon dispersion using a commercial Redstone OSA, with specific relevance to high-precision radial-velocity (RV) spectrograph calibration.  High-resolution transmission spectra of Fabry–Perot etalons are recorded across the visible and near-IR band, enabling precise extraction of the wavelength-dependent spacing of successive resonances and reconstruction of the cavity’s effective dispersion curve. This informs coating designs, as well as strategies to measure the long term drift behaviour of the etalon. As the OSA references the peak measurements back to a reference laser, it provides independent, accurate measurements of the wavelength of each individual mode.

Items.Authors: Hang Zhan, Song-hao Li, Qi Feng, Hong-fei Zhang, Jian Wang
Items.Title: Mechanical design of CMOS camera for irradiation test in space application
Items.Abstract: In modern space exploration missions, CMOS detectors are widely used in scenarios such as astronomical observation and deep-space exploration. They need to work stably for a long time in extreme space environments characterized by low temperature, vacuum, and high radiation. When the detector is exposed in the space radiation environment, irradiation by high-energy particles is likely to cause degradation of its performance. Therefore, it is essential to verify performance of the detector through the irradiation test using a CMOS camera with special design. In this talk, we will present the mechanical design of CMOS camera using GS1517 for Irradiation Test, including the vacuum sealing, support structure for the detector inside vacuum Dewar, Titanium Window and Irradiation Shielding.

Items.Authors: Matthew Ramirez, Hanshin Lee, Uma Subash, Brian L. Vattiat
Items.Title: Mechanical designs, thermo-mechanical tests, laboratory evaluation of the 50-channel pilot absolute multiline system for the Hobby-Eberly Telescope edge sensor upgrade
Items.Abstract: This 25-year old SAMS (Old SAMS) has been showing obsolescence and performance/maintenance deficiencies and hence is undergoing an upgrade. To take the full advantage of this new system and its capabilities, we set out to design the kinematic mounts for the AMS channel components, to evaluate different adhesives for bonding the mounts to the back surfaces of the Zerodur mirror segments, to characterize the overall performance of the pilot AMS, and to assess the dynamic alignment control algorithms and software tools. The adhesive test requires mechanical testing under different environmental conditions that includes thermal cycles and tensile/shear stress. The mirror will also be tilted at 55 degrees to simulate the average tilt angle of mirror segments at the HET. In this paper, we discuss the mechanical designs, thermo-mechanical tests of adhesives, and laboratory evaluation of the 50-channel pilot AMS.

Items.Authors: Dane Zielinski-Nicolson, Christian Schwab, James Downes, David Coutts, Julian Stürmer, Glen Douglass, David Inglis
Items.Title: Metal and alloy IAD mirror coatings for Fabry Perot interferometers used in spectrometer calibration systems
Items.Abstract: This project evaluates whether metal and alloy-based mirror coatings can avoid the chromatic drift observed in dielectric-coated Fabry-Perot interferometers. Using TMM simulations, we identified candidate coating compositions, and we used Ion Assisted Deposition (IAD) to create adhesion layers and alloy cores forming semi-transparent mirrors covering the visible to near-IR. We measured surface roughness with an optical profiler and determined optical constants by ellipsometry. We then built an air-gap etalon and tested it with broadband collimated sources, recording spectra with a high-resolution Fourier-transform OSA. Our IAD metal/alloy coatings produced etalons with broad spectral coverage, and sufficient finesse and throughput.

Items.Authors: Xingda Chen, Jing Luo, Jihong Dong, Xiaohui Zhang
Items.Title: Method to mitigate polarization aberration in astronomical telescopes
Items.Abstract: Due to the demand for high-resolution imaging, polarization aberrations become a critical error source in astronomical telescopes. However, mitigating them involves complex trade-offs with other metrics. Hence, a mitigation method for off-axis three-mirror systems is proposed to address this issue. A multi-objective optimization approach is adopted to minimize wave aberrations and polarization aberrations, with seven core design parameters of such systems treated as free variables. Post-optimization, polarization aberrations are further compensated by introducing plane mirrors, whose orientations are precisely controlled. This compensation is achieved without altering optical design. Typical results show that polarization aberrations are reduced to less than one-eighth of original values, with an average retardance of 0.0046 rad. This method provides insights for polarization aberration mitigation in astronomical telescopes and exhibits broad applicability to other optical systems.
